input

Place a wired mic close to the case or crown. Keep the watch and cable still, away from speakers.

pickup tips

Build power through normal wear or gentle rocking. Light mic contact can help, but avoid rubbing. Keep fabric and tools clear of the movement.

signal

Look for repeating clicks. If pickup is weak, try another contact point. Keep noise reduction and auto gain off.

baseline

Leave the watch still for 60 seconds. Repeat in the same position before adjusting.

Saving needs 32 seconds and two repeatable windows.

adjustment

Save a stable baseline first.
regulator and stud holder

Follow the regulator’s scale pointer: + speeds up, − slows down. Left and right depend on the movement’s rotation. The two-dot end moves opposite the pointer.

There is no fixed seconds/day per nudge. Compare repeatable readings before and after each change.

The stud holder carries the hairspring’s outer attachment and adjusts beat error. Secure it with the correct screw first. A loose or temporarily held stud prevents reliable calibration. Beat error is unsigned, so the reading cannot choose an adjustment direction.

Photograph the starting position. Under magnification, use blunt pegwood on the regulator’s metal edge for a barely visible nudge. Keep the tool clear of the balance and hairspring. Never force a stop. Recheck after closing the case.

Persistent large loss at the + limit, or intermittent stopping, needs inspection.
